jobs.title: Corporate FP&A Manager
jobs.description:
About Snorkel

Snorkel AI is the frontier AI data lab, helping teams build the data and environments behind high-performing frontier and agentic AI. We combine technology with research-driven AI data development to create datasets, benchmarks, evals, and custom solutions for real-world AI systems. Founded out of the Stanford AI Lab in 2019, Snorkel works with leading AI labs and enterprises to move from better data to better outcomes.

Excited to help us redefine how AI is built? Apply to be the newest Snorkeler!

The Role

The Corporate FP&A Manager will own headcount and operating expense planning across Snorkel and serve as the finance partner to department leaders. You will turn hiring and spending plans into reliable forecasts, help teams make investment decisions and build better cost visibility. You will also manage Ramp and procurement workflows and implement planning tools as the business grows.

Key Responsibilities

- Lead annual department budgets and rolling forecasts for headcount and non-headcount expenses, aligning spending with company growth and profitability targets.

- Own the headcount and personnel cost model with People and Recruiting, reflecting hiring plans, attrition, compensation and benefits.

- Partner with department leaders on hiring and investment decisions, identifying cost savings and evaluating tradeoffs in growth, capacity and profitability.

- Partner with Accounting on month-end close, including expense accruals, and lead headcount and OpEx variance analysis against budget and forecast.

- Own SaaS and vendor spend tracking, the purchase order system and procurement approvals, working with Legal, IT and Accounting on purchases and renewals.

- Own and manage Ramp, including spend programs, company cards, approval workflows and expense policies, in partnership with Accounting.

- Implement and administer planning tools such as Pigment or Anaplan and improve data integrations, reporting and planning processes.

- Partner with the Senior FP&A Manager to prepare consolidated financial reporting, with clear commentary on spending trends and outlook for executive reviews and board materials.

About You

- 5+ years of FP&A or business finance experience, including direct ownership of headcount and operating expense planning in a growing technology company.

- Advanced Excel and Google Sheets skills and experience building models that connect hiring, vendor commitments and operating drivers to financial forecasts.

- Hands-on experience managing Ramp, including spend approvals, expense controls and reporting.

- Experience implementing and administering planning systems such as Pigment, Anaplan or similar platforms, including financial model design and data integrations.

- Strong understanding of expense accruals, cost allocation and financial statements, with a record of partnering effectively with Accounting.

- Ability to build relationships with department leaders, explain financial tradeoffs clearly and turn analysis into recommendations.

- Strong attention to detail and the ability to establish practical processes, improve data quality and follow through across multiple workstreams.

Experience with SaaS or AI businesses, IT, cloud or inference costs, and contractor or services delivery economics is a plus.

Why This Role

This role is an opportunity to build the cost planning and spend management foundation of a growing AI company. You will help leaders make better hiring and investment decisions and translate operational improvements into stronger financial performance.
Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Compliance Analyst
jobs.location: New York City, NY (Hybrid); San Francisco, CA (Hybrid)
jobs.description:
About Snorkel

Snorkel AI is the frontier AI data lab, helping teams build the data and environments behind high-performing frontier and agentic AI. We combine technology with research-driven AI data development to create datasets, benchmarks, evals, and custom solutions for real-world AI systems. Founded out of the Stanford AI Lab in 2019, Snorkel works with leading AI labs and enterprises to move from better data to better outcomes.

Excited to help us redefine how AI is built? Apply to be the newest Snorkeler!

Job Description

We are seeking a hands-on, builder-minded Senior Technical Compliance Analyst to serve as the operational engine behind our Trust & Security program.

You will maintain our SOC 2 Type II posture, drive our second entity from Type I to Type II, and act as the bridge between compliance requirements and engineering & delivery execution. You will also lay the technical groundwork to evolve us toward **CMMC 2.0**, ensuring we are ready for federal contracts without slowing down our product velocity.

**This is not a "compliance cop" role.** We practice **"Yes, if..."** security—you will influence architecture, automate policy enforcement, and unblock enterprise sales by ensuring the Security team has pristine, verifiable evidence at their fingertips.

What You will Do

Powering Customer Trust & Revenue Enablement

- The Engine Behind Revenue: Help drafting accurate, technically precise responses to RFPs, security questionnaires (CAIQ, SIG, custom risk assessments), and customer portals.

- Repository Stewardship: Own and continuously update the "Library of Truth"—a pristine repository of pre-vetted security evidence, technical configurations, and policy documents. By keeping this repository audit-ready, you enable the Security team to respond to enterprise prospects in hours, not days.

- Technical Depth on Demand: When a customer asks about AWS KMS encryption, logging pipelines, or IAM privilege escalation paths, you retrieve the granular evidence and draft the written narrative the Security and Legal Team needs to confidently close the deal.

Building Compliance into the DNA

- Compliance Partner: Partner with IT, Security, Product, Engineering, and Delivery early in the development lifecycle. Review new features, infrastructure changes, and vendor integrations to influence architectural decisions that bake in compliance by design—without creating friction or slowing sprints.

- Policy as Guardrails: Write, update, and operationalize security policies that accelerate delivery. Translate abstract SOC 2 and NIST controls into clear, developer-friendly tasks (e.g., IAM hardening, log retention, Zero Trust implementation).

- Compliance-as-Code: Where possible, automate policy enforcement in CI/CD pipelines so that security checks are invisible, automated, and frictionless for engineering teams.

- Enablement, Not Enforcement: Conduct lightweight compliance enablement sessions with engineering teams—showing them how to self-serve evidence collection and interpret compliance requirements—so security becomes everyone's responsibility, not just yours.

Operational GRC & Audit Excellence

- Audit Lifecycle Management: Drive and coordinate the end-to-end SOC 2 Type I and Type II audit cycles across our business entities. Manage audit schedules, coordinate with external auditors, and drive remediation of findings to keep us perpetually audit-ready.

- GRC Automation: Be the power-user of our modern GRC stack (Vanta, Drata). Automate evidence collection, continuously monitor technical controls, and eliminate manual spreadsheet tracking.

- Operational Cadences: Manage the compliance ticketing queue in Jira. Execute routine mandates including quarterly User Access Reviews (UAR), security awareness training, phishing simulations, and managing the Risk Acceptance/Exception process.

- Metrics & Reporting: Build and maintain compliance dashboards (KPIs/KRIs) for the Security Lead and executive team. Track audit readiness scores, remediation SLAs, and control health trends to provide clear visibility into our posture.

- Policy Governance: Manage the annual policy review and attestation cycle—ensuring process owners review, sign off, and update documentation on schedule, keeping our policies evergreen.

Future Federal & Supply Chain Roadmap

- Foundation for Federal Growth: Assist the Security Team in aligning current controls with federal standards—specifically NIST SP 800-53 , NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3 , FedRAMP , and CMMC 2.0 . Help draft early System Security Plans (SSPs) and Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&Ms).

- Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM): Own the third-party vendor review process, assessing critical partners (Cloud, HRIS, CRM) to meet strict federal supply chain requirements and offload this operational work from the Security Lead.

- Incident Readiness: Support the Security Team during security incidents by preserving audit-relevant evidence, documenting the chronology of events, and drafting post-incident reports to satisfy regulatory and audit requirements.

Who You Are

- Experience: 7+ years of experience in technical compliance, IT audit, or GRC within a SaaS or fast-paced startup environment.

- Audit Mastery: Proven end-to-end experience supporting external SOC 2 Type I and Type II audits—with specific expertise auditing IT General Controls (ITGC) (Change Management, Logical Access, System Operations). You know how to manage auditors and translate their requests into actionable developer tasks.

- Technical Acumen: Strong understanding of modern cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP/Azure), IAM, CI/CD pipelines, encryption standards, and vulnerability management. You can read a Terraform plan or an AWS Config rule and interpret its compliance impact.

- Tooling: Experience operating automated compliance platforms (Vanta, Drata), tracking work in Jira, and security awareness platform (KnowBe4)

- Mindset: You are a business enabler . You practice "Yes, if..." security—you negotiate secure alternatives rather than blocking releases or ignoring risks. You thrive in a partnership role, ensuring IT, Security, Engineering, and Delivery teams have everything they need to succeed.

- Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain technical controls to customers and business risks to engineers.

Why Join Us?

- Direct Revenue Impact: Your work directly correlates to revenue. By building the "Library of Truth," you ensure the Security team can close enterprise deals faster and more confidently.

- Be a Builder, Not a Bureaucrat: You won't just check boxes. You will build automated, scalable compliance programs that enable the business to engineer quicker and sell faster.

- Modern, Automated Tooling: Say goodbye to manual spreadsheet tracking. We leverage continuous-monitoring GRC tech so you can focus on technical risk and architecture, not admin overhead.

- Future-Proof Career Growth: Gain rare, hands-on exposure to evolving a commercial SaaS startup into a federal-ready entity (FedRAMP/CMMC), highly accelerating your market value in the GRC space.

**This role is Hybrid Only. 3 days a week in our SF or NYC office.**
Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location.

jobs.title: Finance Manager, DaaS
jobs.description:
About Snorkel

Snorkel AI is the frontier AI data lab, helping teams build the data and environments behind high-performing frontier and agentic AI. We combine technology with research-driven AI data development to create datasets, benchmarks, evals, and custom solutions for real-world AI systems. Founded out of the Stanford AI Lab in 2019, Snorkel works with leading AI labs and enterprises to move from better data to better outcomes.

Excited to help us redefine how AI is built? Apply to be the newest Snorkeler!

About the role

Reporting to the Senior Director of Finance, the DaaS Finance Manager is a critical member of the Finance org and a dedicated finance partner to the DaaS business as we scale.

You will drive the financial insights that lead to better decisions: what we charge, what it costs to deliver, how much we need to deliver, and how it all rolls into revenue and ARR. The job is not just reporting numbers, but telling leadership what they mean and what to do about them.

You will partner closely with the operating teams (Sales, Delivery Ops and RevOps) and bring finance rigor to how we work: clear assumptions, consistent definitions, and models people trust. Success is measured by outcomes, not outputs: deals priced to target margin, staffing plans that match demand, and a forecast leadership has confidence in.

Key responsibilities

The work falls into three pillars, with the mix shifting through the quarter.

1. Revenue model and forecast (with RevOps)

- Maintain the DaaS revenue model: bookings, acceptance-based revenue and ARR by deal, with scenario cases for planning.

- Partner with RevOps on the weekly revenue and ARR forecast, and run the weekly forecast deck and summary for leadership.

- Reconcile the field's call (commit, forecast, best case) with a deal-by-deal finance view; quantify coverage, swing deals and risks.

- Track delivery pacing and acceptance against plan and identify execution risks.

- Build bridges and variance analysis (forecast vs actual, bookings to revenue) for quarterly and annual planning.

- Build the DaaS inputs to the annual operating plan and long-range plan: revenue, cost of delivery, margin and delivery headcount, with monthly actuals-vs-plan variance analysis.

- Partner with Accounting on revenue recognition inputs, COGS and margin actuals.

2. Delivery capacity model

- Run and maintain the delivery capacity model in partnership with Delivery Ops, covering utilization, project mix, headcount per project and cost to deliver.

- Reconcile the capacity plan with actual staffing data and explain variances in mix, productivity and headcount.

- Translate the bookings pipeline into staffing demand and flag hiring or Expert Contributor needs ahead of the quarter.

- Lead a regular capacity planning review with Delivery leadership.

3. Business insights, pricing and strategic projects

- Turn the data into decisions: surface trends in pricing, mix, margin and pacing that leadership has not asked about yet, with a clear recommendation.

- Deal economics: partner with Deal Desk, which owns pricing, as deals need finance input; review deal models and pricing templates for accuracy and margin, and recommend adjustments.

- Customer and product profitability: cost to deliver by customer, project and product, tied to revenue.

- Product economics: what it takes for each product to hit margin targets, and where to invest next.

- Find broken or slow processes and recommend and drive fixes that shorten cycle time and improve data quality.

- Automate what repeats: move recurring models from manual spreadsheets toward scalable, auditable tools.

- Support board and investor content for the DaaS business.

What success looks like

By month six this person runs the weekly forecast and capacity model with the senior leader reviewing rather than building, and Deal Desk and RevOps rely on them to check deal economics.

- First 30 days: Meets the team and learns the DaaS model end to end: pricing, capacity, revenue and ARR. Shadows Deal Desk reviews and the forecast call. Co-produces one weekly forecast deck.

- First 60 days: Runs the weekly forecast deck and summary. Reviews Deal Desk models and templates independently. Leads one monthly capacity review with Delivery Ops.

- First 90 days: Recommends at least one fix to a Deal Desk or RevOps pricing template. Reconciles the capacity model to weekly staffing data with a documented variance bridge. Delivers a first customer or product profitability view.

- First year: Forecast accuracy and pacing calls trusted by the exec team. Margin and capacity assumptions refreshed every quarter without fire drills. Recurring models automated.

Qualifications

We want a builder who is equally comfortable in a deal negotiation thread and a 30-tab model, ideally with experience in a services-heavy, usage-based or manufacturing business.

Must-haves

- 5–8 years in FP&A, product or business finance, deal desk, or strategic finance; at least 2 at a high-growth tech company.

- Hands-on ownership of a revenue forecast and a unit-economics or pricing model, not just review of one.

- Fluency in gross margin vs contribution margin, cost-to-serve, and how pricing, discounting and incentives flow into both.

- Experience with services or labor-based delivery economics: utilization, headcount per project, contractor mix.

- Expert spreadsheet modeling (Google Sheets / Excel) and working SQL; comfortable pulling from a CRM and a data warehouse.

- Clear, concise executive communication: can write a five-line summary leadership can act on.

- Comfort with ambiguity: makes a reasoned call with incomplete data, states the assumptions, and refines as facts arrive.

- Process mindset: spots friction, proposes a simpler way, and drives it to adoption rather than working around it.

- Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, engineering or a related field.

Nice-to-haves

- Experience in AI/ML, data services, a marketplace with reusable inventory (resale economics), services or manufacturing.

- Familiarity with ARR-style metrics and acceptance-based revenue recognition.

- Board or investor materials experience, including fundraise data rooms.

- Uses AI tools and light scripting (Python) to automate recurring analysis.

- Experience with BI tools (e.g., Looker, Tableau) or planning tools (e.g., Adaptive, Pigment).

- Background at a top consulting, banking or finance-rotation program.

Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location.

jobs.description:

Snorkel AI is the frontier AI data lab, helping teams build the data and environments behind high-performing frontier and agentic AI. Excited to help us redefine how AI is built? Apply to be the newest Snorkeler!

About the Team

Snorkel's Marketing team shapes how the AI industry understands frontier data development. We're a team spanning brand, content, communications, product marketing, growth, community, and events, and we work directly with our founders and research team to turn original research into market-defining stories. Brand sits at the center of that work: it's how a data research lab earns attention from frontier labs, Fortune 500 enterprises, top researchers, and the domain experts who contribute to our work.

About the Role

We're hiring a Principal Brand Designer to own the evolution of Snorkel's brand identity. Snorkel has changed faster than its brand has. You'll close that gap: defining where the visual identity goes next, building the system that carries it, and making sure every surface, from the website to a NeurIPS booth to a benchmark leaderboard, looks like it came from the most rigorous lab in AI.

This is a senior individual-contributor role with real leverage and autonomy. You'll be hands-on in the work, and you'll also manage our design agency and a bench of freelance contractors, setting direction, reviewing work, and holding a high bar across everything they ship. This role reports to the CMO.

Responsibilities

- Own the brand identity. Lead the next evolution of Snorkel's visual identity, including logo system, typography, color, illustration, iconography, data visualization, motion, and photography direction.

- Build and govern the brand system. Create and maintain brand guidelines, Figma libraries, templates, and design artifacts that let marketing, sales, research, and recruiting produce on-brand work without a designer in the loop.

- Manage our design agency and contractors. Brief, set creative direction, run reviews, and own quality, scope, timelines, and budget across agency and freelance partners. Decide what gets built in-house versus outsourced, and build the contractor bench as needs grow.

- Design high-visibility launches. Lead creative for major moments, including funding and company announcements, research and benchmark launches, flagship events like our Frontier Data Summit, and conference presence at NeurIPS and other AI venues.

- Make research legible and beautiful. Develop a distinctive visual language for technical content: benchmark results, charts, diagrams, papers, leaderboards, and research blog posts. Partner with researchers so our ideas are as clear visually as they are rigorous.

- Raise the bar across surfaces. Partner with web, content, and product marketing on the website, campaigns, social, sales decks, and event experiences so the brand holds together end to end.

- Set the design operating model. Establish intake, prioritization, review, and approval processes, and introduce AI-assisted design workflows where they make the team faster without lowering quality.

About You

You've shaped a brand. You have strong opinions about craft and can defend them to a founder, a researcher, or an agency creative director – yet you maintain flexibility with letting the brand organically evolve in a dynamic space like AI. You're as comfortable redesigning a logo system as you are giving precise, actionable feedback. You're drawn to technical subject matter and see explaining complex ideas visually as a design problem worth solving. You move fast, you own outcomes, and you raise the standard of everyone you work with.

Requirements

- 8+ years of brand or visual design experience, including in-house brand design at a high-growth technology company.

- A portfolio showing identity or rebrand work you led end to end, plus a broad range of applications: web, campaigns, events, videos, and data visualization.

- Proven experience directing external design agencies and freelancers, including writing briefs, managing scope and budget, and holding partners to a high quality bar.

- Expert craft in typography, layout, color, and composition, with a clear point of view on where brand design for AI is heading

- Deep fluency in Figma and Adobe Creative Suite, and experience building scalable design systems and brand guidelines others actually use.

- Track record leading ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives, influencing senior stakeholders, and making decisions without close oversight.

- Comfort translating technical and research content into clear, compelling visuals.

Bonus

- Experience at an AI, developer tools, or research-driven company.

- Hands-on use of generative AI tools in your design workflow.

- Motion design, 3D, or creative coding skills.
